## Simple explanation

Safety evaluation checks how an AI system behaves in situations where
mistakes could cause harm. It asks not only whether the system works on
ordinary requests, but also how it responds to risky, misleading, or
unexpected inputs.

## Technical explanation

Safety evaluation uses defined hazard categories, test cases, metrics, and
review procedures to assess model and system behavior. Methods may include
adversarial testing, red teaming, policy-compliance checks, human review,
and measurements of harmful output rates. Findings depend on the scope and
coverage of the evaluation.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Pre-deployment testing can reveal failure modes before users encounter
them, while ongoing evaluation can detect regressions and changing risks.
Safety is a system property involving models, tools, data, interfaces, and
operational controls.

## How it works

Teams define intended use, prohibited outcomes, and relevant threat
scenarios. They test representative and adversarial inputs, record outputs
and severity, analyze gaps, and verify mitigations. Results should document
limitations and be repeated after material changes.

## Practical example

A team deploying a support assistant can test whether it reveals private
information, follows malicious instructions in retrieved content, or gives
unsafe advice. Automated tests can be paired with expert review and
production monitoring.

## Common misconceptions

- Passing a fixed test set does not prove a system is safe in every context.
- A model-level refusal test alone does not evaluate tool permissions,
  data access, user experience, or operational safeguards.
